extra.message: Insecure Session Token Allows Authentication Bypass — Unauthorized access to any user's account, including admin, without credentials. [verified: The session token is only base64-encoded without any cryptographic signature (app.py:45). An attacker can decode, modify the username field, re-encode, and set as cookie to impersonate any user; no server-side signature validation exists in the provided code.]

Arbitrary file write leading to remote code execution in log_function_checker — An attacker can achieve remote code execution on the server by overwriting Python files with malicious code, gaining full control of the application. [verified: log_function_checker writes user-supplied log_code and api_code directly to playground/A9/main.py and playground/A9/api.py without sanitization or authentication; these files are imported elsewhere (e.g., line 38 uses main.ssrf_lab), enabling arbitrary code execution when the module is reloaded (e.g., via Django's auto-reload in debug mode).]

Arbitrary file write leading to code execution via user code injection — An attacker can execute arbitrary Python code on the server, leading to full compromise of the application, data exfiltration, and potentially Docker host access. [verified: The function ssrf_code_converter writes user-supplied code (after only trivial line extraction) to a fixed Python file (playground/ssrf/main.py) that is later executed by ssrf_lab. No authentication, input validation, or sanitization exists, enabling arbitrary code execution.]

Hardcoded Django SECRET_KEY — Attacker can forge session cookies, decrypt sensitive data, perform arbitrary signing operations, and potentially impersonate any user or the admin. [verified: The SECRET_KEY is hardcoded in settings.py line 25 with no dynamic override or environment variable fallback, allowing any attacker with source access to forge sessions and decrypt data. No compensating control mitigates this exposure.]

Weak Password Reset Token Generation and Exposure — Account takeover via password reset. [verified: The /reset-password endpoint accepts any email from any unauthenticated user and immediately returns the reset token in a flash message, allowing an attacker to reset any user's password without authorization.]

Pickle Deserialization RCE — Remote code execution on the server, leading to full compromise. [verified: The /deserialize endpoint directly passes user-controlled base64-decoded input to pickle.loads() without any validation, allowing arbitrary Python code execution. No compensating controls exist, and the code path is reachable via POST request.]

Path traversal in SSRF lab — An attacker can read any file on the server filesystem, potentially gaining access to sensitive data (SECRET_KEY, database credentials, flags). [verified: The `ssrf_lab` function uses `os.path.join(dirname, file)` without sanitizing the `file` parameter, allowing path traversal via `../` sequences to read arbitrary files. No compensating controls are present in the provided code.]
